original_value: Automated seizure detection system based on electroencephalograms (EEG) is an interdisciplinary research problem between computer science and neuroscience. Epileptic seizure affects 1% of the worldwide population and can lead to severe long-term harm to safety and life quality. The automation of seizure detection can greatly improve the treatment of patients. In this work, we propose a neural network model to extract features from EEG signals with a method of arranging the dimension of feature extraction inspired by the traditional method of neurologists. A postprocessor is used to improve the output of the classifier. The result of our seizure detection system on the TUSZ dataset reaches a false alarm rate of 12 per 24 hours with a sensitivity of 59%, which approaches the performance of average human detector based on qEEG tools.

result.paraphrase: Automated seizure detection using electroencephalograms (EEG) is an interdisciplinary research topic spanning computer science and neuroscience. Epileptic seizures affect 1% of the global population and can cause serious long-term damage to safety and quality of life. Automating seizure detection can significantly improve patient treatment. In this study, we introduce a neural network model that extracts features from EEG signals using a feature-extraction dimension arrangement method inspired by the traditional approach used by neurologists. A postprocessor is employed to enhance the classifier’s output. On the TUSZ dataset, our seizure detection system achieves a false alarm rate of 12 per 24 hours and a sensitivity of 59%, approaching the performance of an average human detector using qEEG tools.
